title: transform
body:
## transform

Applies a linear transform to the point coordinates: scale, then rotation, then translation, all about the coordinate origin [0, 0, 0]. Vectors and normals are transformed with the geometry (every three-component array while allVectors is true). Polygonal, unstructured and structured grids keep their type; image data and rectilinear grids become an explicit-point dataset. Use it to position, orient or rescale geometry, e.g. scale [0.001, 0.001, 0.001] to convert millimetre coordinates to metres.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Rotation and scaling act about the origin, not the dataset centre, so an object away from the origin also moves. Translate it to the origin first, or use pvTransform with RotateAroundOriginTransform.
- Transformed vector arrays are rotated and scaled too: a millimetre-to-metre scale also multiplies velocity-like vectors by 0.001. Field values are never unit-converted.
- Schemaxis's serial native acceptance run (examples/schemaxis/extended-coverage.json) executes this operation once, translating a sphere by [1, 2, 3]; it does not check this operation's output values, so inspect the result on your own data.

Native constructor: `Transform`. Identity: `curated binding`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. Accepted data: explicit-point datasets (polygonal, unstructured or structured grids) (vtkPointSet); image data (uniform rectilinear grids) (vtkImageData); rectilinear grids (vtkRectilinearGrid). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPointSet","vtkImageData","vtkRectilinearGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `translate` | Displacement [dx, dy, dz] added to every point after scaling and rotation, in dataset coordinate units. Translation does not change vector arrays. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `rotate` | Rotation angles in degrees about the x, y and z axes through the origin [0, 0, 0]. vtkPVTransform composes RotateZ, RotateX, RotateY, so the points are turned about y first, then x, then z (fixed axes), after scaling and before translation. Positive angles follow the right-hand rule about each positive axis. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `scale` | Factors [sx, sy, sz] multiplying the x, y and z coordinates about the origin, applied before rotation and translation. Equal factors change size or units, e.g. [0.001, 0.001, 0.001] for millimetres to metres; unequal factors stretch the geometry. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[1,1,1]` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `allVectors` | If off, only Vectors and Normals will be transformed. If on, all three-component data arrays (considered as 3D vectors) will be transformed. All other arrays won't be flipped and will only be copied. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` | `true` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "transform",
  "inputs": {
    "input": "UPSTREAM_input"
  }
}
```
